providers.surface: Claude Code OAuth live five-hour and weekly usage windows
providers.selectedSource: Preferred OAuth GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage using the current native Claude Code session; optional same-token GET /api/oauth/profile
providers.sourceStatusReason: Unofficial WATCH source: the user approved the CodexBar-style preferred OAuth path plus bounded owner renewal, not CodexBar's full fallback chain. Only claudeAiOauth is eligible; MCP credentials are never accepted or renewed. Token Jar accepts only a successful live usage response as fresh and never directly refreshes, writes, copies, or caches Claude credentials.
providers.credentialPersistence: Claude-owned ~/.claude/.credentials.json and native Keychain generic-password service Claude Code-credentials with the account fixed to NSUserName(); Token Jar keeps no app-owned Claude credential cache and does not directly persist, copy, write, or refresh either store
tokenTankIO: Read claudeAiOauth from ~/.claude/.credentials.json; a valid AI record is authoritative. If the AI record is absent, including a valid MCP-only file, query only the native generic-password service Claude Code-credentials AND account NSUserName(), matching Claude Code's current OS-user account. Never fall back to another same-service account. A present malformed, wrong-scope, or invalid-expiry AI record fails closed without Keychain fallback; MCP tokens are never accepted or renewed. If both stores are MCP-only, return missing with the source-login action

Require a finite positive expiry and user:profile scope; evaluate expiry only after each potentially slow credential read completes. Do not scan other files, services, accounts, browser stores, or arbitrary inherited environment variables; the owner safeEnvironment supplies only the canonical OS account identity for USER and LOGNAME, using the same NSUserName() value for both

GET only https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and optionally the same-token /api/oauth/profile with bearer authorization, JSON headers, anthropic-beta oauth-2025-04-20, and User-Agent claude-code/2.1.0

Map 401/403 to honest authentication failure, apply 429 backoff, and retain only a prior in-memory snapshot as stale on network, timeout, or schema failure; only a successful live usage response marks a snapshot fresh

Locked/off-console collection skips native Keychain. Otherwise serialize native calls on one bounded utility worker per reader: 5 seconds background, 120 seconds manual to allow human password or biometric entry; do not start another query while a timed-out call remains unresolved and discard any late result. A timeout establishes only that no result arrived within the bound, not that approval was declined

ClaudeNativeKeychainAccess serializes process-wide native queries. Background access temporarily applies SecKeychainGet/SetUserInteractionAllowed(false) and always restores the previous process-local policy on success or error; it never changes item ACLs or user Keychain settings. Manual access never enables interaction when the inherited process policy was already disabled

Explicit manual Refresh may read native Keychain only when unlocked/on-console and, only for an expired native token, launch an allowlisted Claude executable in an empty mode-0700 temporary directory with --safe-mode --tools '' --allowed-tools '' --setting-sources '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'; the safeEnvironment supplies USER and LOGNAME from the same canonical NSUserName() value rather than arbitrary inherited environment. Strip ANSI CSI layout before exact readiness/trust/status matching, send /status, accept only the current exact empty-workspace question 'Is this a project you created or one you trust?' or the reviewed older exact question, and deny unknown prompts. Then reread and require a changed fresh token

Do not import browser cookies, scrape PTY usage output, call the Admin API or any LLM inference endpoint, fall back to ~/.claude.json cachedUsageUtilization, or directly refresh/write/copy/cache a Claude token
externalPaths: native Keychain generic-password service Claude Code-credentials; account NSUserName() only
providers.tccClass: none; a native Keychain access prompt is permitted only during explicit manual Refresh
providers.liveValidation: Controlled owner CLI comparison proved the old sanitized environment lacked USER/LOGNAME and falsely reported loggedIn=false; canonical NSUserName() values restored loggedIn=true, and the production /status touch completed in about 1.28 seconds. This status touch does not prove automatic rotation of a naturally expired token. Native metadata-only QA then proved service-only Keychain matching selected a different OS account; service plus kSecAttrAccount=NSUserName() selected the intended account. Native lookup now pins both fields, with 27 native-session tests passing, including same-service account isolation and no broadening when the current account is missing. The correct account's token was read successfully, but the live API returned 401 authentication_error with a revoked indication for both tested User-Agent versions; this was provider authentication failure, not missing native approval. The user explicitly authorized the official claude --safe-mode auth login --claudeai flow, which exited 0 after browser approval. After reauthentication, an exact-account direct OAuth usage GET returned 200 with numeric five_hour and seven_day utilization, reset strings, limits, and extra_usage present. Frozen local-v4 manual Refresh showed fresh Claude usage percentage and account label; restarting the same approved binary produced a fresh background cold start with usage and account and no native prompt observed. The plan UI was not verified because its accessibility identifier was absent. Latest full package evidence is 168 tests across 12 suites, the native total is 27, the post-fix app suite passed 35 tests, the post-fix full UI suite passed 19 tests, and the universal Release build succeeded. Independent local-v4 checks confirmed the feed and archive Ed25519 signatures, archive length and SHA-256, and graceful app termination. Local-v1/v2/v3 are obsolete; local-v4 remains a dirty-source QA artifact and none may be published.
providers.mutationRisk: Token Jar does not directly mutate Claude credentials, item ACLs, or user Keychain settings. Explicit manual Refresh may let Claude Code mutate its own native store; recovery requires a changed fresh token. Native Keychain calls are serialized and bounded; timed-out late data is discarded and no replacement query starts until the old call resolves. Background interaction disablement is process-local and always restored. The owner runner remains dedicated-process-group, 15-second/256-KiB bounded, with an empty mode-0700 workdir removed afterward and no raw TUI persistence.
providers.releaseBlocker: For v0.1.10, the user explicitly accepted prerelease publication with natural-expiry changed-token renewal, real upgrade, physical Intel, and clean/quarantined-host checks disclosed as unverified. Official interactive re-login, live HTTP 200, frozen local-v4 manual and background cold-start collection, final app/UI tests, and independent local-v4 signature/archive checks are verified. Do not infer automatic expiry renewal from /status or re-login. Source CI and clean-revision rebuild, payload/signature/checksum audits, and remote release/feed verification remain mandatory. Local-v1/v2/v3 are obsolete; no dirty-source QA artifact may be published.

providers.selectedSource: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json OIDC session; when access expiry is within 60 seconds or the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, refresh_token grant at fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token and atomic same-file rotation, then one proxy retry; primary cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits; only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, bearer-only POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same session bearer and a 6-second timeout
providers.sourceStatusReason: The Grok CLI owner session and CLI-proxy credits endpoint remain primary. Unlike CodexBar, which is only a reference for credits behavior and does not directly refresh OAuth, Token Jar performs the user-approved narrow renewal: an OIDC access token expiring within 60 seconds, or one rejected by the first proxy request with 401/403, is renewed once through the official fixed token endpoint after exact issuer and selected client/scope checks; the rotated session is atomically preserved to the same owner file before one proxy retry. Only a successful proxy snapshot with unknown usage may trigger the existing same-session bearer-only gRPC-web billing fallback. Proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity remain authoritative; web billing supplies usage only. Token Jar never imports browser cookies, uses Grok ACP stdio or a CLI subprocess, offers manual-token UI, calls the xAI Management prepaid-balance API, or caches tokens in Keychain.
providers.rejectedAlternative: Browser-cookie imports, Grok ACP stdio, CLI subprocess or interactive automation, manual-token UI, local-session estimates, xAI Management API/prepaid-balance calls, Keychain token caches, backups, other secret stores, and arbitrary credential copying remain prohibited. The older Grok Build ACP x.ai/billing probe returned JSON-RPC -32601 (method-not-found) on official Grok 1.0.13.
providers.credentialOwner: Grok CLI, with user-approved Token Jar renewal of the selected OIDC entry
providers.credentialPersistence: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json; Token Jar may atomically replace only that same file after a successful official refresh_token grant, preserving the optional rotated refresh token and updated expires_at; no backup, copy, or other secret store
tokenTankIO: Open only ~/.grok/auth.json through the Grok-scoped session capability; require issuer https://auth.x.ai and exact agreement between the selected client/scope suffix and the entry's non-empty oidc_client_id

When expires_at is within 60 seconds, or only after the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, POST a refresh_token grant to fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token with public-client authentication, no cookies, and no redirects

Once renewal starts, hold a bounded token-free lock shared only by Token Jar processes across the current-file reread, HTTP rotation, conflict comparison, and same-file persistence; preserve the response's optional rotated refresh token and updated expiry in the selected entry, prefer an observably newer external session, and replace through a same-directory mode-0600 temporary file. Observer cancellation does not interrupt the shared transaction: a canceled observer receives CancellationError after commit; cancellation before renewal starts aborts. Grok CLI is not assumed to honor the lock.
HTTPS GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with the selected ephemeral bearer; after 401/403 renewal, retry this proxy exactly once

Only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same selected bearer, a 5-byte empty gRPC-web data frame (00 00 00 00 00), no cookies, and a 6-second timeout

Preserve proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity; adopt a published web percentage, or an omitted proto3 scalar as zero only for a structurally complete response with a recognized current weekly/monthly period containing the refresh time; otherwise retain unknown, including a failed fallback
Expose published creditUsagePercent or the same-row on-demand used/cap ratio under the credits quota
Display only the selected auth entry's optional email in memory; never infer identity from another entry or token
providers.liveValidation: Historical evidence: on 2026-09-07 a current-host read-only probe reproduced HTTP 200 proxy credits with no creditUsagePercent, onDemandUsed/onDemandCap both zero, and currentPeriod present; the production Swift adapter plus URLSessionNetworkClient returned used 0%, remaining 100%, and preserved proxy reset through a validated active-period proto3 implicit zero from bearer-only web billing. The 97 package tests reported then cover the pre-renewal implementation. Latest evidence after the final USER/LOGNAME and Keychain-account pinning changes: the full package suite passed 168 tests in 12 suites, the app suite passed 35 tests, and the full UI suite passed 19 tests. Thirteen release-tool tests, Provider I/O audit, forbidden FileTimestamp API check, independent integration review, and rotation review pass 2 passed in the earlier run. A token-safe current-host production GrokOAuthSessionProvider probe on 2026-09-11 forced exactly one renewal with rejectedAccessToken set to the current token, then fetched usage through the real GrokAdapter: access token changed, refresh token rotated, saved token matched the returned session, expiry was in the future, file mode was 0600, noncredential metadata was preserved, usage fetch succeeded with one quota and available usage percentage, and account identity matched the session. No secret was printed or copied. This does not prove a naturally expired-token event, real HTTP 401/403 injection, concurrent real Grok CLI rotation, packaged final release, another OS, CI, or notarization.
providers.mutationRisk: The only credential mutation allowed is successful Grok renewal written atomically to the same ~/.grok/auth.json through a same-directory mode-0600 temporary file. A bounded token-free lock covers reread, HTTP rotation, comparison, and persistence among Token Jar processes; once renewal starts it settles despite observer cancellation, after which a canceled observer receives CancellationError after commit, while pre-start cancellation aborts. Comparison detects observable external rotation and prefers a newer session but cannot close the final rename window against an uncooperative concurrent Grok CLI writer; the lock is not claimed to be CLI-honored. No backup, other secret store, cookie import, Management API fallback, or unrelated source-store mutation is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: WATCH: live-validate a naturally near-expiry event, real proxy HTTP 401/403 renewal, concurrent real Grok CLI rotation, missing/revoked versus network-error recovery, and the packaged final candidate on supported OS versions; complete CI, signing, and notarization evidence
